standard.title: Linear Expressions
standard.description: create, expand, factorise, rearrange and simplify linear expressions, applying the associative, commutative, identity, distributive and inverse properties
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can formulate algebraic expressions and apply the distributive property informally (from AC9M7A02). Students understand variables, constants and operations in expressions.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students fluently expand, factorise, rearrange and simplify linear expressions, applying algebraic properties explicitly.

nodes.label: Expanding and simplifying linear expressions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students expand brackets in linear expressions using the distributive property and collect like terms to simplify.
nodes.minimum_width: Expand and simplify a linear expression with one set of brackets (e.g. 3(2x + 4) − x).
nodes.typical_width: Expand and simplify expressions with multiple brackets and negative coefficients; identify and collect like terms; use algebra tiles or area models to verify.
wider: Investigate the distributive property across subtraction: verify that a(b − c) = ab − ac using substitution and area models.
Explore common student errors in expansion (e.g. 3(x + 2) = 3x + 2) — explain why the error occurs and how to avoid it.

response_modes.reason: Expanding and collecting like terms is a procedural skill requiring fluency before factorisation and rearrangement. Errors in sign handling with negative coefficients are the primary failure point.

nodes.hinge_reason: Expansion errors — particularly sign errors with negative coefficients — propagate directly into Node 2 (factorisation requires recognising expanded form) and Node 3 (rearrangement requires reliable expansion to verify). Students who cannot expand fluently cannot check their factorisation or rearrangement by expanding back.
success_criteria: Correctly expands brackets including those with negative coefficients.
Does not partially distribute (e.g. only multiply the first term).

nodes.label: Factorising linear expressions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students factorise linear expressions by identifying the highest common factor and express as a product of the HCF and a bracket.
nodes.minimum_width: Factorise a linear expression with an integer HCF (e.g. 6x + 9 = 3(2x + 3)).
nodes.typical_width: Factorise linear expressions with variable and integer common factors; verify by expanding; understand factorisation as the inverse of expansion.
wider: Investigate the relationship between factorisation and GCD from number — connect algebraic HCF to numerical HCF.
Explore factorising expressions with negative leading terms — develop a convention for handling negative HCF.

response_modes.reason: Factorisation requires an explicit search strategy: identify the HCF of all terms, divide each term, write the bracket. Students who approach factorisation without a structured method miss common factors or introduce errors.

nodes.hinge_reason: Factorisation is required within Node 3 rearrangement (isolating a variable from multi-term expressions requires recognising common factors) — students who cannot factorise reliably cannot complete the rearrangement steps that depend on it.
success_criteria: Identifies the HCF of all terms in a linear expression.
Verifies by expanding back to the original expression.

nodes.label: Rearranging linear expressions
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students rearrange linear expressions and formulas using inverse operations and algebraic properties, maintaining equivalence.
nodes.minimum_width: Rearrange a two-term linear expression to isolate a specified variable.
nodes.typical_width: Rearrange multi-term linear formulas to make any variable the subject; apply commutative and inverse properties explicitly; verify by substitution.
wider: Apply rearrangement to real formulas from science and everyday contexts: rearrange distance = speed × time for speed; rearrange area formulas for dimensions.
Investigate how rearrangement connects to solving equations — express the connection between 'rearranging a formula' and 'solving for a variable' explicitly.

response_modes.reason: Rearranging formulas requires simultaneous application of expansion, factorisation, and inverse operations — integrating all prior nodes in this descriptor.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Rearranging real formulas from science and engineering contexts is a rich application for advancing students — the connection between formula rearrangement and solving equations is a significant algebraic insight.
success_criteria: Correctly rearranges a linear formula to make a specified variable the subject.
Applies inverse operations in the correct order.
Verifies the rearranged formula by substitution.
